findings.message: Scope in has no `ownership` YAML block. The established pattern (tests/test_seeded_phase3_11.py `_yaml(...)['ownership']`, and phase3-continue-12's pinned block) reads the owns-then-hooks contract of the emitted seeds from the authoring continuation's Scope in. Without it, 'pin owns-then-hooks fences' has nothing to be checked against. The registry gives restart-timers `squatch/restart.py`, `squatch/timers.py`, `tests/test_restart_timers.py` plus the 'daemon/CLI composition roots' shorthand, and the ticket never resolves that shorthand to exact hook paths.
findings.paved_road: Add a Scope in YAML `ownership` block: restart-timers owns [squatch/restart.py, squatch/timers.py, tests/test_restart_timers.py] and hooks the exact composition-root paths (e.g. squatch/daemon.py, squatch/__main__.py, plus any reconcile/drain path that reap-before-dispatch forces). phase3-continue-14 owns [tickets, tests/test_seeded_phase3_14.py] with hooks []. Add a criterion requiring the seeded test to assert that block against the emitted fences and NEW_PATH_OWNERS (including tests/test_seeded_phase3_14.py -> phase3-continue-14).

findings.message: The acceptance criteria omit predecessor-test closure. Section 20 requires every continuation to check it, and phase3-continue-12's criteria carry it as a pinned phrase. Restart-timers hooks the daemon and CLI composition roots, so existing composition, control-CLI, and heartbeat tests may carry negative or local contracts it must migrate or preserve. Right now only Definition of rejected mentions predecessor closure, and no criterion forces the check.
findings.paved_road: Add a criterion: tests/test_seeded_phase3_13.py checks predecessor-test closure for restart-timers. Every existing test whose asserted behavior restart-timers must migrate is fenced, and every one it must preserve is read-only Context, not a fence entry.

findings.message: Context embeds only tests/test_seeded_phase3_11.py. It carries none of the existing composition-root surfaces that the emitted restart-timers seed must fence and embed (squatch/daemon.py, tests/test_daemon_composition.py, the then-existing composition harness required by section 20, tests/test_control_cli.py). phase3-continue-12 embedded exactly these surfaces for the same reason. Without them the implementer cannot establish the fence partition, the on-demand exceptions, or the authoring-time sizes from evidence. The base render is 33,408 chars against a 120,000-char headroom, so there is room to embed them.
findings.paved_road: Add the existing composition-root surfaces to Context (squatch/daemon.py, tests/test_daemon_composition.py, tests/test_control_cli.py, and squatch/__main__.py or an explicitly named on-demand exception if the render measurement requires it). Name them in Scope in and the criteria the way phase3-continue-12 does, and keep heartbeat's not-yet-merged paths out of Context.

findings.message: 'Pin their exact identities, dependency edges, tiers, budgets' gives no values. The registry marks restart-timers ALONE KNOWN-DEEP (high/high) and continuations medium/medium. The edges (restart-timers after phase3-continue-13, phase3-continue-14 after restart-timers, following the pattern in test_seeded_phase3_11's BATCH) are not stated, so the pins cannot be checked against the ticket.
findings.paved_road: State the exact values in Scope in: restart-timers depends [phase3-continue-13], high/high. phase3-continue-14 depends [restart-timers], medium/medium. Both source seed, state confirmed, P1, Plan contract section 20, expected 75m / stuck 150m within drain.max_ticket_minutes, and batch size within seeding.max_seeds_per_admission.
